justification: Three changes on the path that decides what regulatory text is served. Two fix the extraction splitter, which was handing a whole page to a section that starts partway down it -- serving a parking rule as a stormwater rule. The third makes the commit worker read fidelity_status, which it had never read at all: the one check that compares our output against the council's own PDF could not stop a single write.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_review_queue (fidelity_status, suspect_reason, created_at, status) and regulatory_provisions. No schema change and no new table. information_schema.columns was read for BOTH tables rather than assumed: fidelity_status exists only on dcp_review_queue, and regulatory_provisions has no equivalent -- which is what forces the fidelity guard to be absolute rather than before/after like the two beside it.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Four in this change, each caught by measuring rather than reasoning. (1) I said the 13 Northern Beaches fidelity failures were a two-column problem; measured, only 1 of 13 was, 7 were headings starting mid-page and 3 were not on the cited page at all. (2) I assumed the legibility guard would catch phrase-level interleave; its worst single-letter ratio across 124 rows was 0.055 against a 0.20 threshold -- 'clean' -- while C3 Parking continued into 'G7 - Evergreen Introduction'. (3) I read the 8 remaining section_collapsed failures as data loss; comparing TOTAL text showed the chapter going 49 rules/537,845 chars -> 113 rules/528,636 chars, i.e. -1.7% -- it is being re-split finer, and a per-row size heuristic cannot see that. (4) My own first version of the heading fix cut the body past every line the title-continuation loop had absorbed, which DELETED a short first sentence ('C2 Setbacks' / 'The front setback is 6m.' lost the setback). A test written for something else caught it.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: split_page_at_headings already exists for MULTI_HEADING_COUNCILS and handles SEVERAL headings per page. It is deliberately one council wide -- its own comment says widening it 'must not be done without measuring the council first' -- and it is not widened here. The mid-page fix sits inside its per-segment loop, so a pre-split council reaches it with match.start() == 0 and behaves exactly as before. The remaining Northern Beaches C3/G7 defect IS a multi-heading page and is left for that route, measured, rather than bolted onto this one.
pre_impl.external_source_error: None -- no network. The extraction was re-run against the real chapter from R2 (273 pages, 23.5 MB) and the before/after compared in the live queue.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Both directions. Too loose and a section serves the previous section's text as its own -- C4 Stormwater opened with 'End of trip facilities are not required for schools', a parking rule published as a stormwater control. Too strict and the fidelity guard refuses ordinary re-reads, at which point it gets switched off; the bar is therefore read off the measured distribution and a confusable negative is pinned at 1.7%. The worst outcome for the guard specifically is a third one: appearing to run while grading nothing, which is what reading batch_ts from the dry-run branch would have caused.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A section starting mid-page is handed the whole page again; the text above such a heading is dropped from the section it belongs to; the heading is left in the body as well as the title; a short first sentence is swallowed into the title and lost from the body; the previous section is not credited with the page it shares; the commit worker stops calling enforce_fidelity, or calls it with a batch timestamp resolved inside the dry-run branch; the fidelity bar leaves the gap the distribution shows; ungraded rows start counting as failures or as passes; 'grounded' is treated as a failure; the batch scope or the approved-status filter is dropped from the fidelity query; or --allow-section-loss starts doubling as --allow-fidelity.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 15 mutations planted, 15 caught. On the splitter (5/5): whole page to the new section, heading left in the body, previous section not credited with the shared page, leading text discarded, and the no-leading-text branch claiming the page. On the fidelity guard (10/10): guard not called, > became >=, bar moved to 20% and to 1%, ungraded counted as failures, grounded counted as a failure, batch scope dropped, size floor removed, stale batch_ts from the dry-run branch, and an override that ignores the chapter name. Full suite 6,627 passed / 2 skipped. Verified against production rather than only in tests: re-extracting northern_beaches/warringah-dcp-2011-full took its failed rows 13 -> 11, and C4 Stormwater went from opening with C3 Parking's tail to opening with its own text.

functions.name: page_tail (in _extract_sequential)
functions.input: One page of text and the regex match for a section heading found on it.
functions.output: The text from the END of the heading down -- the part belonging to the section starting here. The text above it is appended to the section already open, and that section keeps the page.
functions.if_none: No heading on the page means page_tail is the whole page and it extends the open section, which is the common case and is unchanged.

functions.name: enforce_fidelity
functions.input: A cursor inside the open transaction, the council, the chapter, the created_at of the run being committed, and the set of chapters a person has named.
functions.output: (graded, bad, detail), or raises FidelityRefused so the caller rolls back and keeps the approval.
functions.if_none: No graded rows means the gate never looked. It prints that it is not judging and lets the commit proceed -- refusing every ungraded chapter would stop the pipeline dead -- but an unchecked batch must not read as a clean one, so the abstention is stated rather than silent. A test pins the message.

functions.name: judge_fidelity
functions.output: True to refuse. Split out from the DB access so the thresholds can be driven directly by the real run figures.
functions.if_none: Under FIDELITY_MIN_GRADED rows it returns False: one bad row in ten is 10% and means nothing.

values.name: FIDELITY_MAX_BAD_RATIO = 0.05
values.value: The share of a batch that may fail source verification
values.why: Read off the distribution, not chosen. Across all 62 extraction runs holding >=20 graded rows the failure fraction runs 0.0 x22 ... 2.4, 2.7, 3.8, then jumps to 6.1, 6.2, 8.3, 10.5, 16.9, 18.5, 21.1, 23.1, 26.1, 30.2. The per-rule view agrees independently: comparing only rules present in both of two consecutive runs of one chapter, regressions run 0.4, 0.4, 1.3, 1.4, 1.7, 1.8, 2.9, 4.3, then 8.6, 18.5, 23.1, 30.2. Both have their widest gap in the same place and 5% sits inside it.
values.if_missing: A bar picked by feel either refuses ordinary re-reads until someone disables the guard, or sits above the bad cluster and never fires.
values.read_at: scripts/dcp_supersede_guard.py -- FIDELITY_MAX_BAD_RATIO, with both distributions written out above it.

values.name: FIDELITY_PASSING = (grounded, ok)
values.why: 'grounded' is the BEST outcome -- verified against the source page -- and 'ok' means the insert-time row checks found nothing. NULL is excluded from both numerator and denominator: counting ungraded rows as bad would make the guard fire hardest on the chapters nobody has checked.
values.source: dcp_fidelity_gate.gate_chapter writes grounded/flagged; classify_row_fidelity writes ok/failed. Queue totals 2026-09-20: ok 7,493, grounded 5,437, NULL 450, flagged 137, failed 114.
values.if_missing: An approval script written earlier in this same session used `IS DISTINCT FROM 'ok'` and turned 81 grounded rows into failures. A test pins the inverse.

queries.purpose: The graded rows of the one extraction run this commit would publish.
queries.where_clause: council = %s AND chapter_key = %s AND created_at = %s AND status = 'approved' AND fidelity_status IS NOT NULL. The created_at scope matters because a chapter's queue holds every run it has ever had -- northern_beaches alone carries six batches -- and the worker commits ONE run whole.

break_it.scenario: The fidelity guard is given a batch timestamp resolved inside the dry-run branch.
break_it.what_happens: That branch ends in `continue`, so on the commit path the name is either undefined or left over from the PREVIOUS chapter. The guard would query another chapter's run, find no rows, print 'not judged' and pass -- appearing to run while grading nothing, which is worse than not running.
break_it.how: The lookup is hoisted above the dry-run split and happens exactly once per chapter. A test asserts the assignment precedes `if dry_run:` and that there is only one of them.

break_it.scenario: A whole chapter is refused because every row looks 'collapsed'.
break_it.what_happens: Exactly what northern_beaches does: 8 of 11 failures are section_collapsed because the extraction re-split 49 giant rules into 113 properly-sized ones. Nothing is lost -- total text moved -1.7% -- but a per-row size heuristic cannot see that, and a blind --allow-fidelity would follow.
break_it.how: The refusal says so, and says how to check: compare TOTAL text, not row sizes. A test asserts that wording is in the message.

break_it.scenario: Removing the heading from the body also removes the section's first sentence.
break_it.what_happens: The title-continuation loop folds any following line under 50 characters into the heading. A first version of this fix cut the body past everything the loop had absorbed, so 'C2 Setbacks' / 'The front setback is 6m.' kept the title and LOST the setback -- a control silently deleted.
break_it.how: Only the matched heading is removed; continuation lines stay in the body. Repeating a title fragment is untidy, deleting a setback is a wrong answer served as regulation. Tested at both sides of the 50-character cap.

break_it.scenario: The remaining northern_beaches failures are read as the same defect.
break_it.what_happens: They are not. Of 11: 8 are section_collapsed false positives on a finer re-split, 2 are junk section codes ('21' keyed off a permit number, 'R2' off a control marker), and 1 is C3 Parking still continuing into 'G7 - Evergreen Introduction' -- a page holding TWO headings, which the single-match path cannot fix.
break_it.how: Not addressed here. The multi-heading route is split_page_at_headings, which is opt-in per council and whose own comment requires measuring the council before widening it. That measurement is a separate run.

break_it.scenario: The legibility guard is assumed to cover this.
break_it.what_happens: It does not and cannot. Its signature is the fraction of words that are a single letter, which sees GLYPH interleave. Two columns read across each other produce entirely correct words in the wrong order and score near zero: 0.055 worst case on the chapter whose fidelity gate failed 13 of 124.
break_it.how: The two checks are now separate and both run. The guard's own comment says which class each covers, and the module docstring no longer implies the ratio is a general corruption detector.

post_merge.db_reset: No. Nothing here writes. The 14 Ku-ring-gai rows approved during this work were a separate queue-status change with its own CSV backup, and the commit worker has not been run.
post_merge.manual_verify: Re-run the northern_beaches extraction after merge and confirm the failed-row count holds at 11 or below; the 13 -> 11 measurement was taken from this branch.
